say.en: In a modern bottling plant, bottles are filled, capped, labelled and checked without anyone touching them. A few people watch screens. How is this different from a worker running a machine? In this lesson: Define automation.
Distinguish automation from mechanisation and computerisation.
Identify the elements of an automated system.

body.en: *Automation* is the use of machines, controls and information technology to carry out a process with little or no human intervention. An automated system senses what is happening (sensors), decides what to do according to a program (controller or computer) and acts (actuators, motors, robots), correcting itself through feedback. People design, program, maintain and monitor the system rather than doing each step.

points.en: Little or no human intervention in each step
Elements: sensors, a controller, actuators and feedback

body.en: Mechanisation replaces human muscle with machines, but a person still operates and controls each machine. Computerisation means using computers to store and process information and to support tasks such as accounting or billing; it may or may not run the process itself. *Automation* goes further: it replaces both human effort and human control of routine steps. Robotics and artificial intelligence are tools of advanced automation: robots perform physical tasks, and AI handles tasks that need judgement, such as reading documents or answering queries.

points.en: Mechanisation: machines do the work, people control them
Robotics and AI: advanced forms of *automation*

prompt.en: Sort each example: mechanisation, computerisation or automation?

text.en: A worker drives a tractor to plough a field
A tailor uses an electric sewing machine
A shop keeps its accounts in accounting software
A clerk types student records into a database
A drip system waters crops when soil sensors read dry
Robots weld car bodies on an assembly line
A bank's system sends a payment reminder on the due date by itself

explanation.en: If a person still runs the machine, it is mechanisation; if computers only hold and process data, it is computerisation; if the process senses and acts by itself, it is automation.

problem.en: A dairy fills milk pouches. Method A: workers fill pouches by hand. Method B: a filling machine fills a pouch each time a worker presses a pedal. Method C: a level sensor stops the filler at 500 ml, a sealer seals, a camera rejects leaking pouches. Classify the methods.

steps.en: A: people do and control the work: manual.
B: a machine does the work, but a person controls each cycle: mechanisation.
C: sensors, a controller and feedback run the cycle without a person: automation.

answer.en: A is manual, B is mechanised and C is automated.

A: people do and control the work: manual.
B: a machine does the work, but a person controls each cycle: mechanisation.
C: sensors, a controller and feedback run the cycle without a person: automation.
So the answer is A is manual, B is mechanised and C is automated.

body.en: If a person must start or stop every cycle, it is mechanisation. If the system decides by itself from sensor readings, it is automation.
